page: Amazon Web Services x8i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 24 physical cores with hyper-threading, utilizing the x86_64 architecture on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The CPU includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for deep learning operations. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory and processing capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core execution, image processing, and text processing. Memory performance is characterized by a strong read-only cached bandwidth of 3831.46 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier. Computational benchmarks show strong results in Passmark CPU tests, software compilation, and cryptography. For database and key-value workloads, the system demonstrates strong performance with 90.13 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and high database operations scores.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core and strong database performance, the x8i.12xlarge is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data processing. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM prompt processing, though text generation speeds for larger models remain average due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider for I/O-heavy applications.
